gloss: closing a business; going out of business

definitions.gloss: closing a business; going out of business; ceasing operations
definitions.explanation: The act of permanently shutting down a business or professional practice. Can refer to voluntary closure (such as retirement) or forced closure due to financial difficulties.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}を{廃業|はいぎょう}する。
examples.english: To close the shop for good.

examples.japanese: {後継者|こうけいしゃ}がいなくて{廃業|はいぎょう}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: With no successor, they decided to close the business.

examples.japanese: この{商店街|しょうてんがい}では{廃業|はいぎょう}する{店|みせ}が{年々|ねんねん}{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: In this shopping street, more and more shops are going out of business every year.

notes:
Refers to permanently ceasing business operations. Unlike a temporary closure, {廃業|はいぎょう} implies a final, definitive end to a business. It is a significant social issue in Japan, particularly with aging business owners in rural areas who have no one to take over.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {廃業|はいぎょう}する: to close a business, to cease operations
- {廃業|はいぎょう}{届|とどけ}: notice of business closure (filed with authorities)
- {廃業|はいぎょう}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる: to be driven out of business
- {廃業|はいぎょう}{率|りつ}: closure rate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {閉店|へいてん}: closing a shop (can be temporary or permanent; more casual)
- {倒産|とうさん}: bankruptcy, business failure (implies financial collapse)
- {休業|きゅうぎょう}: temporary closure, suspension of business
